# runtime-bridge-conflict-resolver (reference summary)

## Purpose
Diagnose MCP bridge conflicts (Path 1 Official Blender Lab MCP 5.1+ vs Path 2 mcp-for-blender, port 9876 collisions, host mismatch) and hand off to official-runtime-readiness-checker.

Resolve the single-bridge constraint when more than one MCP runtime path is configured against the same Blender instance (or when ports collide). Blender accepts only one MCP bridge session per instance (default port 9876) — so running Path 1 (Official Blender Lab MCP 5.1+) and Path 2 (community `mcp-for-blender`, renamed from `ahujasid/blender-mcp`) concurrently, connecting two MCP clients to one Blender instance, colliding on port 9876, or enabling both Path 1 host (a) and host (b) on one session causes inconsistent signals.

## Metadata & truth boundary
- **Canonical skill:** `skills/runtime-bridge-conflict-resolver/SKILL.md`
- **Contract:** `skills/runtime-bridge-conflict-resolver/contract.json` (`v1.0.0`)
- **Category / role:** `runtime-and-execution` / `port-and-addon-conflict-resolver`
- **Capability tier:** `L0`
- **Truth-state policy:** Runtime status defaults to `Not Run`; Artifact status defaults to `Not Produced`; mutation rule is `downgrade_only` (never upgrade without verified evidence).

## When to use
- `official-runtime-readiness-checker` reports inconsistent signals (e.g. host reports connected but tool calls return the wrong tool surface)
- both Path 1 (Official Blender Lab MCP 5.1+) and Path 2 (community `mcp-for-blender`, renamed from `ahujasid/blender-mcp`) add-ons are enabled in the same Blender instance
- two MCP clients are pointing at the same Blender instance (e.g. Claude Desktop with Connector + Cursor with manual MCP)
- Path 1 host (a) and host (b) are both active on a single session
- log or port output shows a collision on default port `9876`

## Trigger cues
- "tool surface looks wrong"
- "smoke test passed yesterday but recipe fails today"
- "Lab MCP and ahujasid both installed"
- "Claude Desktop and Cursor both pointing at Blender"
- "port 9876 already in use"
- "single-bridge constraint violation"

## When not to use
- no readiness signal yet (run official-runtime-readiness-checker first) → delegate to `official-runtime-readiness-checker` (`references/skills/official-runtime-readiness-checker.md`; run official-runtime-readiness-checker first)
- no runtime path has been chosen yet → delegate to `runtime-path-picker` (`references/skills/runtime-path-picker.md`; route to runtime-path-picker)
- the user wants to switch or set up a path from scratch → delegate to `official-runtime-setup-guide` (`references/skills/official-runtime-setup-guide.md`; route to official-runtime-setup-guide)
- the bridge matrix is clean and only one path is active, but smoke tests still fail → delegate to `blender-troubleshooting` (`references/skills/blender-troubleshooting.md`; route to blender-troubleshooting)
- the user explicitly wants both paths configured for separate Blender instances on different ports (requires explicit port isolation) → delegate to `official-runtime-readiness-checker` (`references/skills/official-runtime-readiness-checker.md`; requires explicit port isolation)

## Inputs & output/evidence contract
### Required inputs
- `target_blender_instance` (`string`): Running Blender session identifier or binary path experiencing bridge or port collisions
- `configured_mcp_hosts_and_addons` (`object`): Inventory of enabled Blender add-ons (Lab MCP vs mcp-for-blender) and active MCP client connections

### Optional inputs
- `port_9876_diagnostics` (`string`): Optional socket/port binding diagnostics around default port 9876

### Primary outputs
- `bridge_conflict_diagnosis_matrix`
- `single_bridge_isolation_steps`
- `post_resolution_readiness_recheck_route`

## Quick-start procedure
1. list every active / configured bridge for the target Blender session
2. check for port collision (commonly `localhost:9876`)
3. identify which path is intended; which is residual
4. propose the cheapest disable / port-isolation step
5. hand off to `official-runtime-readiness-checker` to re-verify

## Handoff notes
- **[upstream_reference]** When official-runtime-readiness-checker reports inconsistent signals → `official-runtime-readiness-checker` (`references/skills/official-runtime-readiness-checker.md`)
- **[fallback]** If the bridge matrix is clean but failures persist → `blender-troubleshooting` (`references/skills/blender-troubleshooting.md`)
- **[upstream_reference]** If the user wants to change paths or set up a path → `official-runtime-setup-guide` (`references/skills/official-runtime-setup-guide.md`)
- **[upstream_reference]** If the intended runtime path has not been chosen yet → `runtime-path-picker` (`references/skills/runtime-path-picker.md`)

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- **Runtime boundary:** This skill never disables add-ons, edits MCP client configs, changes ports, kills processes, or runs Blender. It only diagnoses the conflict, proposes the cheapest resolution for the operator to perform, and hands off to `official-runtime-readiness-checker`.
- Disabling add-ons, editing MCP client configs, changing ports, killing processes, or running Blender
- Upgrading Runtime or Artifact truth states
- Replacing `official-runtime-readiness-checker`, `runtime-path-picker`, `official-runtime-setup-guide`, or `blender-troubleshooting`
